title: Protesters clash with police in Paris and across France over living costs
seoTitle: Paris clashes over living costs and schools

tea.why: Protesters are demonstrating against the high cost of living, school funding shortages, and rising prices.
tea.want: Demonstrators demand better school funding, higher wages, and improved pensions.
tea.changed: Oct 28: Authorities reported that nationwide arrests exceeded 1,200 following widespread clashes and urban unrest.

summary: Hundreds of thousands of people took to the streets in Paris and across France for mass protests demanding better school funding and addressing the high cost of living. The demonstrations, which organizers estimated drew up to 800,000 participants and the Interior Ministry estimated at over 400,000, saw peaceful marches turn into clashes near their endpoints. Masked individuals threw projectiles, fireworks, and homemade bombs at police officers, who responded with tear gas, sound grenades, and water cannons. The unrest led to extensive property damage, shop closures, and record arrests nationwide. President Emmanuel Macron and Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu condemned the violence, blaming extremist groups and criminals for sowing chaos, while interior officials deployed thousands of security personnel.
response: Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez announced a massive security deployment of up to 70,000 officers. Authorities condemned the violence, and President Emmanuel Macron warned that those who attacked prefectures and shops would be punished.

crowd.text: more than 400,000 people rallying across France

arrests.text: Nationally, according to authorities, arrests have exceeded 1,200

deaths.text: A protester who took to the streets yesterday in Paris against the high cost of living died of cardiac arrest.

updates.text: Clashes erupted in Paris and across France as nationwide marches drew hundreds of thousands over living costs and school funding.
The French retail chamber reported that store turnover in downtown protest areas plummeted by 80 percent.
Authorities announced that nationwide arrests surpassed 1,200 amid reports of a protester's death from cardiac arrest and severe injuries.
